1.q: Which statement BEST matches how PRINCE2 defines a project?
o: A temporary organization set up to deliver one or more business products in line with an agreed business case
A permanent team set up to run and continually improve an organization's routine business operations
A temporary structure set up to lead several related projects so that outcomes are achieved progressively
The whole of an organization's investment in the changes it needs to meet its strategic objectives
1.w: PRINCE2 defines a project as a temporary organization created to deliver one or more business products according to an agreed business case (see manual 1.3). The two defining ideas are that it is temporary and that it is justified by a business case.

n.1: Running and improving routine operations is business as usual, which is permanent; a project is temporary and ends once its change is in place.
n.2: Leading several related projects to achieve outcomes progressively describes a programme, which is the context a project may sit within, not a project.
n.3: An organization's total investment in change to meet strategic objectives describes a portfolio, not an individual project.

1.q: A project manager explains that her organization's projects use the PRINCE2 processes and management products, but the project board has decided not to apply the 'manage by exception' principle. How should this project be viewed?
o: It is a PRINCE2 project, because the processes and management products are in use
It is a PRINCE2 project, because principles may be tailored to suit the project's scale
It is not a PRINCE2 project, because all seven principles must be applied
It is not a PRINCE2 project, because every management product must be used unchanged
1.w: The principles are the guiding obligations of the method: unless all seven are applied, the project is not being run as a PRINCE2 project, however many processes or products it uses (see manual ch 2 and 1.2).

n.0: Using processes and management products is not enough: a project that leaves out any principle is not a PRINCE2 project (manual ch 2).
n.1: Tailoring adapts processes, practices, roles, management products and terminology; the principles themselves are not tailored away (manual 2.7).
n.3: Management products can be merged, split, renamed or reformatted when tailoring, so unchanged use is not a requirement (manual 2.7).

1.q: Which statement best describes the 'tailor to suit the project' principle?
o: Delegated authority is limited by setting tolerances against plans
The method is adapted to the project's size, complexity and risk
The project concentrates on defining and delivering its products
The project is planned, monitored and controlled stage by stage
1.w: The 'tailor to suit the project' principle means the method is applied and adapted to the project's environment, size, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability and level of risk (see manual 2.7).

n.0: Setting limits of delegated authority through tolerances describes the 'manage by exception' principle, not tailoring (manual 2.5).
n.2: Defining and delivering products and their quality requirements describes the 'focus on products' principle (manual 2.6).
n.3: Planning, monitoring and controlling stage by stage describes the 'manage by stages' principle (manual 2.4).

1.q: In PRINCE2, which term describes the existing organizations connected with a project (the business, users and suppliers), each with its own structures, governance, culture and people?
o: Organizational ecosystem
Project ecosystem
Project management team structure
Business layer
1.w: The organizational ecosystem is the set of existing organizations, such as the business, users and suppliers, each bringing its own structures, governance, culture and people (see manual 3.1, fig 3.1).

n.1: The project ecosystem is the temporary set of people, relationships, structures and ways of working created for the project, not the existing organizations (manual 3.1).
n.2: The project management team structure is the set of project roles (board, project manager, team managers, assurance and support), not the wider organizations (manual 6.2.3).
n.3: The business layer is the commissioning level that provides the mandate and appoints the executive; it is one part of the organizational ecosystem, not the whole of it (manual 6.2).

1.q: In the PRINCE2 people element, which statement defines management?
o: Motivating people to achieve the project's objectives through persuasion and influence
Instructing the execution of tasks in line with the agreed ways of working
The set of shared attitudes, values, goals and practices that shape how people behave
Representing the business, user and supplier interests when directing the project
1.w: PRINCE2 defines management as instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working, which is distinct from leadership (see manual 3.3).

n.0: Motivating people through persuasion and influence describes leadership, not management (manual 3.3).
n.2: Shared attitudes, values, goals and practices describe culture, not management (manual 3.2.3).
n.3: Representing the three project interests is what the project board does at the directing level; it is not the definition of management (manual 6.2.4).

1.q: Which management product sets out the direction and scope of the project and, together with the current stage plan, acts as the 'contract' between the project manager and the project board?
o: Project brief and initiation stage plan
Project initiation documentation
Business case
Project mandate
1.w: The PID gives the direction and scope of the project and, with the stage plan, forms the agreement between the project manager and the project board. It is assembled in initiating a project and its authorized version is baselined (see manual 4.3.1).

n.0: The project brief and initiation stage plan are approved in authorize initiation so that initiation can start; the brief is then superseded by the PID, which is the agreement used for delivery (manual 5.5, 14.4.1, 4.3.1).
n.2: The business case documents the business justification (costs against benefits and risks); it is one part of the PID rather than the overall agreement on direction and scope (manual 5.5).
n.3: The project mandate is the trigger for starting up a project, provided by the business layer; it is not a PRINCE2-created agreement between the project manager and the board (manual 13.3).

1.q: Which statement describes the purpose of the organizing practice in PRINCE2?
o: To establish mechanisms to judge whether the project is, and remains, desirable, viable and achievable
To facilitate communication and control by defining the products to be delivered and the means to deliver them
To define and establish the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities
To establish mechanisms to monitor and compare actual achievements against those that were planned
1.w: The organizing practice exists to define and establish the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities, often summarized as the 'who' of the project (see manual 6.1).

n.0: Judging whether the project is and remains desirable, viable and achievable is the purpose of the business case practice (manual 5.1).
n.1: Defining the products and the means to deliver them, to aid communication and control, is the purpose of the plans practice (manual 7.1).
n.3: Monitoring and comparing actual achievements against those planned is part of the purpose of the progress practice (manual 11.1).

1.q: Which statement describes the purpose of the plans practice?
o: To support communication and control by defining the products and the means of delivering them
To capture the user's requirements for the products and set up how those requirements will be met
To provide a means of judging whether the project is, and stays, desirable, viable and achievable
To compare actual achievement with what was planned and forecast the work still to be done
1.w: The plans practice exists to support communication and control. It defines what is to be delivered (the products) and the means of delivering it: who, how and where, with estimates of when and how much, so that the business case is satisfied (see manual 7.1).

n.1: This is the purpose of the quality practice, which deals with user requirements and how they will be met, not with defining the means, timing and cost of delivery (manual 8.1).
n.2: This is the purpose of the business case practice, which supports decisions on continued investment; the plan must satisfy the business case but does not judge it (manual 5.1).
n.3: This describes the progress practice, which compares achievement with the plan; the plans practice provides the plan that progress is measured against (manual 11.1).

1.q: Which statement describes the purpose of the quality practice in PRINCE2?
o: To establish mechanisms to judge whether the project is, and remains, desirable, viable and achievable
To identify, assess and control uncertainty so that the project's chances of success are improved
To document the user's requirements of the project's products and establish the means by which they will be met
To establish mechanisms to monitor actual achievements against those planned and to control any deviations
1.w: The quality practice exists to document what the user requires of the project's products and to establish how those requirements will be met, so that the products are fit for purpose (see manual 8.1).

n.0: Judging whether the project is and remains desirable, viable and achievable is the purpose of the business case practice (manual 5.1).
n.1: Identifying, assessing and controlling uncertainty is the purpose of the risk practice (manual 9.1).
n.3: Monitoring actual against planned achievement and controlling deviations is the purpose of the progress practice (manual 11.1).

1.q: What is the purpose of the risk practice?
o: To collect and assess issues and control changes to the project's baseline, so keeping the agreed products under control
To identify, assess and control uncertainties that would affect the project's objectives, so improving its ability to succeed
To establish mechanisms to judge whether the project is and remains desirable, viable and achievable, so supporting decisions
To define and implement the means by which the project will verify that its products are fit for use, so meeting expectations
1.w: The risk practice exists to identify, assess and control uncertainty that would affect the project's objectives, and in doing so it improves the project's ability to succeed (see manual 9.1).

n.0: This is the purpose of the issues practice, which deals with events relevant to the project and with changes to the baseline, not with uncertainty about objectives (manual 10.1).
n.2: This describes the business case practice, which supports decisions about investment; the risk practice controls uncertainty affecting objectives (manual 5.1, 9.1).
n.3: This describes the quality practice, which deals with quality specifications and fitness for use rather than with uncertain events (manual 8.1, 9.1).

1.q: A project manager briefs a new project board on handling issues. Which statement describes the purpose of the issues practice?
o: To identify, assess and control uncertainties that could affect the project's objectives
To compare actual achievement with the plan and control deviations that cause an exception
To collect and assess issues and to control changes made to the project's baseline
To document the user's requirements for the products and establish how they will be met
1.w: The issues practice collects and assesses issues and controls changes to the project baseline, so that change happens in a managed way rather than by drift (see manual 10.1).

n.0: Identifying, assessing and controlling uncertainties is the purpose of the risk practice, which deals with events that have not yet happened (manual 9.1).
n.1: Comparing actual with planned achievement and controlling deviations is the purpose of the progress practice (manual 11.1).
n.3: Documenting user requirements and the means of meeting them is the purpose of the quality practice (manual 8.1).

1.q: A new project manager asks why PRINCE2 includes a progress practice. Which statement describes the purpose of the progress practice?
o: To set up ways to judge whether the project is, and remains, desirable, viable and achievable, so that decisions on continued investment can be made
To support communication and control by defining the products to be delivered and the means, timing and cost of delivering them
To identify, assess and control the uncertainties that could affect the project's objectives, improving its ability to succeed
To set up ways to monitor and compare actual achievement with the plan, forecast objectives and viability, and control deviations causing an exception
1.w: The progress practice exists to provide mechanisms for monitoring and comparing actual against planned achievement, to forecast the project's objectives and continued viability, and to control deviations that would cause an exception (see manual 11.1).

n.0: Judging whether the project is and remains desirable, viable and achievable is the purpose of the business case practice (manual 5.1), not progress.
n.1: Defining the products and the means to deliver them, to support communication and control, is the purpose of the plans practice (manual 7.1).
n.2: Identifying, assessing and controlling uncertainty is the purpose of the risk practice (manual 9.1).

1.q: A new project board asks which PRINCE2 process its members will use. Which process does the project board use from the end of starting up a project until after the project has been closed?
o: Controlling a stage
Managing a stage boundary
Directing a project
Initiating a project
1.w: Directing a project is the project board's process. It runs from the request to initiate at the end of starting up a project until after closing a project, when the board authorizes closure (see manual chapter 12, fig 12.1).

n.0: Controlling a stage is used by the project manager at the managing level to run each delivery stage day to day; it is not the board's process (manual 12, 16.1).
n.1: Managing a stage boundary is used by the project manager near the end of each stage to prepare the information the board needs; it is a managing-level process (manual 12, 18.1).
n.3: Initiating a project is run by the project manager during the initiation stage to build the project's foundations; it is a managing-level process (manual 12, 15.1).

1.q: Which statement describes the purpose of the 'controlling a stage' process?
o: To control the link between the project manager and the team manager for specialist work
To give the board enough information to review the stage and confirm continued justification
To assign and monitor work and take corrective action to keep the stage within tolerance
To provide a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed
1.w: Controlling a stage exists so the project manager can assign work, monitor it, deal with issues, report progress to the project board and take corrective action, keeping the stage within the tolerances the board has set (see manual 16.1).

n.0: This is the purpose of managing product delivery, the team manager's view of work packages, not the project manager's control of the whole stage (manual 17.1).
n.1: This describes managing a stage boundary, which is used at or near the end of a stage rather than to run the work within it (manual 18.1).
n.3: This is the purpose of closing a project, which confirms acceptance of the project product within the final stage (manual 19.1).

1.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. A project is a [?] organization that is created to deliver one or more business products according to an agreed business case.
o: permanent
temporary
line
commercial
1.w: The PRINCE2 definition describes a project as a temporary organization (see manual 1.3). It exists to deliver business products under an agreed business case and is no longer needed once the change has been made.

n.0: A permanent organization is the business as usual structure; a project is set up for a limited time and then closed.
n.2: The line organization runs business as usual; a project creates its own temporary organization alongside it.
n.3: A commercial customer and supplier relationship is one possible project context, not part of the definition of a project.

1.q: Why does PRINCE2 give guidance through principles rather than prescribing exactly how the method should be fitted to each project?
o: So that the method can be applied differently to suit each project, even within one organization
So that every project in an organization follows an identical set of processes and documents
So that the project board can choose during initiation which principles suit the project
So that the method can take the place of the specialist techniques used in each industry
1.w: Because the method is guided by principles rather than prescriptive rules, it is flexible enough to be applied in different ways on different projects, including projects in the same organization (manual ch 2).

n.1: Principles exist precisely so that projects do not all have to look identical; the method is applied differently to suit each project (manual ch 2).
n.2: The board does not choose principles: all seven must be applied for the project to be a PRINCE2 project (manual ch 2).
n.3: PRINCE2 does not replace specialist or industry techniques; it is a project management method that works alongside them (manual 1.1).

1.q: Which is a purpose of tailoring PRINCE2?
o: To decide which of the seven principles the project will apply
To replace the business's own processes with PRINCE2 processes
To move accountability from the executive to the project manager
To make the method used appropriate to the project and its context
1.w: One purpose of tailoring is to make the project management method appropriate to the project, for example by aligning it with the business processes that govern and support the project (see manual 2.7).

n.0: All seven principles must be applied for a project to be a PRINCE2 project; tailoring adapts the method, not the principles (manual ch 2, 2.7).
n.1: Tailoring aligns the method with the business processes that govern and support the project rather than replacing them (manual 2.7).
n.2: The executive's accountability cannot be delegated, and tailoring does not move it to the project manager (manual 6.2.4).

1.q: Which statement describes the project ecosystem in PRINCE2?
o: The permanent structures and governance of the business that commissioned the project
The temporary people, relationships, structures and ways of working set up for the project
The list of stakeholder groups and the frequency with which each receives information
The hierarchy of all work to be done, linking the product breakdown to work packages
1.w: The project ecosystem is temporary: it is the people, relationships, structures and ways of working created for the project where the business, user and supplier interests meet (see manual 3.1, fig 3.2).

n.0: Permanent structures and governance belong to the organizational ecosystem, which exists before and after the project (manual 3.1).
n.2: Stakeholder groups and how often they receive information are set out in the communication management approach, not the project ecosystem (manual 3.4).
n.3: A hierarchy of all work linking the product breakdown structure to work packages is the work breakdown structure (manual 6.2.5).

1.q: According to PRINCE2, how is leadership on a project best carried out?
o: Through the formal authority of the project board over each team member
Through detailed instructions issued by the project manager to each team
Through collaboration across the project ecosystem
Through the line management structure of the business layer
1.w: PRINCE2 says leadership on projects is best done through collaboration across the project ecosystem, because temporary project leaders often lack formal authority over the people involved (see manual 3.3).

n.0: Project teams are temporary and span organizations, so formal authority is harder to exercise; leadership relies on collaboration and influence rather than board authority (manual 3.3).
n.1: Issuing instructions for tasks to be carried out is management, not leadership (manual 3.3).
n.3: Project teams draw people from several organizations, so the business layer's line structure does not cover them; leadership works through collaboration (manual 3.3, 3.3.1).

1.q: Which set of records is held in the project log?
o: The daily log, the lessons log, the issue register and the nine management approaches
The business case, the project plan, the risk register and the quality register
The highlight reports, the checkpoint reports, the issue register and the lessons log
The daily log, the lessons log, and the issue, risk, quality and product registers
1.w: The project log is the dynamic record of the project. It holds six records: the daily log, the lessons log and the issue, risk, quality and product registers (see manual 4.3.2).

n.0: The management approaches belong in the PID, not the project log; the project log holds the daily log, lessons log and four registers (manual 4.3.1, 4.3.2).
n.1: The business case and the project plan are baselined products in the PID; only the registers listed belong in the project log (manual 4.3.1, 4.3.2).
n.2: Highlight and checkpoint reports are progress reports, not project log records; the log holds the daily log, lessons log and four registers (manual 4.3.2, 11.5).

2.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.

The organizing practice defines and establishes the project's structure of [?] and responsibilities, which PRINCE2 describes as the 'who' of the project.
o: accountability
communication
deliverables
tolerances
2.w: The purpose of the organizing practice is to define and establish the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities (see manual 6.1).

n.1: Communication with stakeholders is planned through the communication management approach in the people element; it is not the structure the organizing practice establishes (manual 3.4, 6.1).
n.2: Deliverables (products) are the 'what' of the project, defined through the plans and quality practices, not the 'who' (manual 7.1).
n.3: Tolerances are the permitted deviations set at each level of management under the progress practice, not what the organizing practice structures (manual 11.2).

2.q: A plan answers several questions about how a project will deliver its products. Which question is answered by the business case rather than by the plan?
o: What products are to be delivered
Why the products are worth delivering
Who will deliver the products, and how
When the products will be delivered
2.w: The plans practice defines the what, who, how, where, when and how much. The why is held in the business case, which the plan must satisfy (see manual 7.1).

n.0: Defining the products to be delivered (the what) is a core part of the plan's purpose (manual 7.1).
n.2: The means of delivery, including who and how, are defined in the plan (manual 7.1).
n.3: The plan contains estimates of when products will be delivered, as well as how much they will cost (manual 7.1).

2.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.

The quality practice documents the user's [?] of the project's products and establishes the means by which they will be met, so that the products are fit for purpose.
o: requirements
benefits
tolerances
dependencies
2.w: The purpose of the quality practice is to document the user's requirements of the project's products and to establish how they will be met (see manual 8.1).

n.1: Benefits are the measurable improvements the business case practice justifies and tracks; the quality practice is about what the products must be like (manual 5.1, 8.1).
n.2: Tolerances are the permitted deviations set under the progress practice; quality tolerance is one tool of the quality practice, not what it documents from the user (manual 11.2, 8.2.1.2).
n.3: Dependencies between products are identified by the plans practice when sequencing the work, not documented as the user's needs (manual ch 7).

2.q: Which statement best describes what the risk practice can achieve for a project?
o: It guarantees that the agreed objectives will be met by removing the uncertainties before delivery starts
It resolves events that have already happened and are now affecting the project's approved baseline
It improves the ability of the project to succeed by controlling the uncertainties that affect its objectives
It confirms at each stage boundary that the project is still desirable, viable and achievable
2.w: Controlling uncertainty improves the chance of success, but the agreed objectives cannot be guaranteed: some uncertainty always remains (see manual 9.1).

n.0: The risk practice cannot guarantee that objectives will be met; it improves the ability to succeed by managing uncertainty throughout the project (manual 9.1).
n.1: Events that have already happened are issues, handled by the issues practice; risks are uncertain events that may happen (manual 9.1, 10.1).
n.3: Confirming that the project remains desirable, viable and achievable is the role of the business case practice, although risks feed into it (manual 5.1).

2.q: How does the issues practice in PRINCE2 7 relate to change control?
o: Issue management in PRINCE2 7 encompasses change control, so the issues practice controls changes to baselines
Change control now sits in the change management approach, which the people element uses to manage baselines
Change control is a separate eighth practice that takes over once an issue has been assessed and recommended
Change control is handled by the quality practice because it concerns the quality specifications of products
2.w: In PRINCE2 7, issue management includes change control: the issues practice replaced the old change theme and covers controlling changes to the project baseline (see manual 10.1).

n.1: In PRINCE2 7 change management means organizational transition under the people element; it is not the control of baselines (manual ch 3, 10.1).
n.2: There are seven practices; change control is part of the issues practice rather than a practice of its own (manual ch 4, 10.1).
n.3: The quality practice defines and checks quality requirements; controlling changes to approved products belongs to the issues practice (manual 8.1, 10.1).

2.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.

As well as comparing what has been achieved with what was planned, the progress practice provides a [?] for the project's objectives and its continued viability.
o: baseline
tolerance
justification
forecast
2.w: Part of the purpose of the progress practice is to provide a forecast for the project's objectives and its continued viability, so that problems can be seen before they happen (see manual 11.1, 11.2.5).

n.0: A baseline is an approved, version-controlled product (such as a plan) used as a reference point; the progress practice compares against it rather than providing one for viability (manual 4.3, 11.1).
n.1: Tolerances are the permissible deviations set by each management level; they are not what the practice provides for objectives and viability (manual 11.2.1).
n.2: Justification of the investment is judged through the business case practice (manual 5.1); progress feeds forecasts into it rather than providing the justification itself.

2.q: Starting up a project is unusual in the PRINCE2 process model because more than one management level takes part in it. Which levels are involved in starting up a project?
o: The directing and the managing levels
The managing and the delivering levels
The directing and the delivering levels
The delivering level and the business layer
2.w: Starting up a project is used by both the directing level (the executive appoints the project management team after being appointed by the business layer) and the managing level (the project manager prepares the outline business case, brief and initiation stage plan) (see manual chapter 12, fig 12.1).

n.1: Team managers at the delivering level do not take part in starting up a project; delivery work starts with managing product delivery in later stages (manual 12).
n.2: The delivering level is not involved in starting up a project, and the project manager at the managing level does most of the preparation work (manual 12, 13.4).
n.3: Team managers are not involved, and the business layer sits outside the project management team; it appoints the executive but is not a management level of the project (manual 12, 6.2).

2.q: The 'controlling a stage' process is used throughout each delivery stage. Which role carries out its activities day to day?
o: The project manager, within the stage tolerances set by the board
The team manager, within the work package tolerances set by the project manager
The executive, within the project tolerances set by the business layer
Project assurance, on behalf of the board members it reports to
2.w: Controlling a stage sits at the managing level: the project manager assigns and monitors work and keeps the stage within the stage tolerances set by the project board (see manual 12, 16.1).

n.1: The team manager works in managing product delivery, accepting and executing work packages; controlling a stage is the project manager's process (manual 12, 17.3).
n.2: The executive directs through directing a project and manages by exception; the board does not run the stage day to day (manual 14.3).
n.3: Project assurance checks the project for the board members, independently of the project manager; it does not run the stage's activities (manual 6.2.4).

2.q: According to PRINCE2, what happens when the change that a project was created to introduce has been implemented?
o: The project team becomes the new line management structure for the changed operations
The project carries on as a programme so that the expected benefits can be realized
Business as usual resumes in its new form and the need for the project ends
The project moves into a further delivery stage to maintain the products it has built
2.w: Projects are temporary: once the desired change has been implemented, business as usual resumes in its new form and the need for the project is removed (see manual 1.3). The project is then closed.

n.0: The project team is temporary and is disbanded at closure; running the changed operations is a business as usual responsibility.
n.1: A project does not turn into a programme when it finishes; benefits realized after closure are reviewed by the business, not by a continuing project.
n.3: Maintaining products after handover is business as usual work; a project closes within its final stage rather than adding a stage for maintenance.

2.q:
Which two statements about the PRINCE2 principles are correct?
1. They are guiding obligations and good practices.
2. They may be left out on small, low-risk projects.
3. They are shown as the foundation beneath the practices, people and processes.
4. They are replaced by the practices once the project has been initiated.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4
1 and 3
2.w: Statement 1 is correct: the principles are guiding obligations and good practices. Statement 3 is correct: the integrated elements figure shows the principles as the foundation, with the practices, people and processes built on them (manual ch 2, fig 1.1).

n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: small projects still apply all seven principles; it is the method, not the principles, that is scaled down by tailoring (manual 2.7).
n.1: Statements 2 and 4 are both wrong: principles are never left out, and the practices put the principles into effect rather than replacing them (manual ch 2).
n.2: Statement 4 is wrong: the principles apply throughout the project lifecycle and are not replaced by the practices after initiation (manual ch 2).

2.q: A project board agrees that a small, low-risk project will have shorter, less frequent highlight reports than the organization's large projects. Which purpose of tailoring does this serve?
o: Fitting project controls to the project's scale, complexity and risk
Aligning the method with the business processes governing the project
Making sure no more work is done than the agreed products need
Making sure lessons from earlier projects reach the lessons log
2.w: One purpose of tailoring is to make project controls fit the project's scale, complexity, importance, team capability and risk; the frequency and formality of reports and reviews is the typical example (see manual 2.7).

n.1: Aligning the method with business processes is the other purpose of tailoring, but the change here is to the frequency and formality of a project control (manual 2.7).
n.2: Doing no more work than the agreed products need is part of the 'focus on products' principle, not a purpose of tailoring (manual 2.6).
n.3: Capturing lessons from earlier projects belongs to the 'learn from experience' principle, not to adjusting reporting (manual 2.2).

2.q:
Identify the missing word(s) in the following sentence.

The project ecosystem is formed where the [?] ecosystems intersect.
o: programme, portfolio and project
directing, managing and delivering
business, user and supplier
executive, manager and team
2.w: PRINCE2 shows the project ecosystem as the intersection of the business, user and supplier ecosystems, the three project interests (see manual 3.1, fig 3.2).

n.0: Programmes and portfolios are possible contexts for a project, not the three ecosystems whose overlap forms the project ecosystem (manual 1.5, fig 1.2).
n.1: Directing, managing and delivering are levels of the project management team, not ecosystems (manual 6.2, fig 6.2).
n.3: Executive, project manager and team manager are roles; the project ecosystem is formed from the business, user and supplier interests (manual fig 3.2).

2.q: Which statement best explains the difference between leadership and management on a PRINCE2 project?
o: Leadership is the responsibility of the project board, while management belongs to the project manager
Leadership is needed during initiation, while management is needed during the delivery stages
Leadership sets the agreed ways of working, while management motivates people to follow them
Leadership motivates and influences people, while management directs tasks to agreed ways of working
2.w: Leadership is about motivating, persuading, influencing and co-creating; management is about instructing tasks in line with agreed ways of working. Projects need both throughout (see manual 3.3).

n.0: PRINCE2 does not split the two by level: the project manager must lead people as well as manage tasks, and board members also lead (manual 3.3).
n.1: Both are needed throughout the project lifecycle; neither is tied to particular stages (manual 3.3).
n.2: This reverses the concepts: motivating people is part of leadership, while management instructs tasks within the agreed ways of working (manual 3.3).

2.q:
Identify the missing word(s) in the following sentence.
The [?] is the dynamic record, kept up to date throughout the project, that holds the daily log, the lessons log and the project's registers.
o: project log
project initiation documentation
project brief
product register
2.w: The project log is the second of the two containers for most management products: a dynamic record holding the daily log, lessons log and the issue, risk, quality and product registers (see manual 4.3.2).

n.1: The PID is the other container: an aggregation of baselined products (business case, approaches, plan and so on) used to authorize the project, not the dynamic log (manual 4.3.1).
n.2: The project brief is created in starting up a project as the foundation for initiation; it does not hold the logs and registers (manual 5.5).
n.3: The product register is one of the records held inside the project log; it does not contain the daily log or lessons log (manual 4.3.2).

2.q: Which practice establishes who is accountable for the project, who has the authority to direct it and who is responsible for each area of its management?
o: Plans
Progress
Business case
Organizing
2.w: Organizing is the practice that sets out the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities, including the project board's authority to direct and the project manager's day-to-day responsibility (see manual 6.1, 6.2).

n.0: Plans defines the products and the means to deliver them (what, how, where, when, how much); it does not establish the accountability structure itself (manual 7.1).
n.1: Progress establishes mechanisms to monitor actual against planned performance and to control deviations, not the structure of accountability (manual 11.1).
n.2: Business case establishes mechanisms to judge whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable; it does not define who is accountable for what (manual 5.1).

2.q:
Identify the missing word(s) in the following sentence.
A plan defines the products to be delivered and the means of delivering them, so that the [?] of the project is satisfied.
o: project product description
quality management approach
business case
risk management approach
2.w: The plans practice defines the what and the means of delivery in order to satisfy the business case, which holds the why (see manual 7.1).

n.0: The project product description describes the major products and their acceptance; it is one input to planning, not the justification the plan must satisfy (manual 7.5).
n.1: The quality management approach sets out how quality will be managed; the plans purpose refers to satisfying the business case (manual 7.1, 8.5).
n.3: The risk management approach describes how risks will be managed; the plan's targets must satisfy the business case (manual 7.1, 9.5).

2.q: A new hospital outpatients project is being set up. Which practice is concerned with documenting what the users need from the project's products and establishing how the project will meet those needs?
o: Plans
Business case
Progress
Quality
2.w: Documenting the user's requirements of the products and establishing the means of meeting them is the purpose of the quality practice (see manual 8.1).

n.0: Plans defines the products to be delivered and the means, timing and cost of delivering them; it does not document the users' quality requirements (manual 7.1).
n.1: Business case judges whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable; it does not set out what the users need from each product (manual 5.1).
n.2: Progress monitors actual against planned performance and controls deviations; it does not document the users' requirements (manual 11.1).

2.q:
Identify the missing word(s) in the following sentence.
The purpose of the risk practice is to identify, assess and [?] uncertainties that would affect the project's objectives.
o: eliminate
control
transfer
accept
2.w: The risk practice identifies, assesses and controls uncertainty, which improves the project's ability to succeed (see manual 9.1).

n.0: Uncertainty cannot be eliminated from a project; the practice controls it, and it cannot guarantee the objectives will be met (manual 9.1).
n.2: Transfer is one of the response types for an individual risk, used for passing financial impact to a third party; it is not part of the practice's purpose (manual 9.2.3.1).
n.3: Accept is one of the response types for an individual risk; the purpose of the practice is to control uncertainty, not to accept it (manual 9.1, 9.2.3.1).

2.q:
Identify the missing word(s) in the following sentence.
The purpose of the issues practice is to collect and assess issues and to control changes to the project's [?], so that the products the board has approved are not altered without authority.
o: risk profile
baseline
tolerances
benefits
2.w: The issues practice controls changes to the project baseline: the current approved versions of the management and project products that are subject to change control (see manual 10.1).

n.0: The risk profile is assessed in the risk practice; it is not what the issues practice controls changes to (manual 9.1).
n.2: Tolerances are set by the level above under manage by exception; changing them is not the purpose of the issues practice (manual 2.5, 11.2.1).
n.3: Benefits are defined and tracked in the business case practice; the issues practice controls changes to approved products (manual 5.1, 10.1).

2.q: Which element of the purpose of the progress practice is concerned with looking ahead, rather than reviewing what has already been achieved?
o: Comparing the achievements made so far with those that were originally planned
Recording lessons in the lessons log as soon as they are identified
Providing a forecast for the project's objectives and continued viability
Defining the products to be delivered and estimating when they will be ready
2.w: Forecasting is the forward-looking element of the progress purpose: it predicts the project's objectives and continued viability so that deviations can be dealt with early (see manual 11.1, 11.2.5).

n.0: Comparing actual with planned achievement is part of the purpose, but it reviews work already done rather than looking ahead (manual 11.1).
n.1: Recording lessons is part of the guidance on reviewing progress and lessons, not part of the purpose of the progress practice (manual 11.1, 11.2.3).
n.3: Defining products and estimating when they will be delivered is the purpose of the plans practice, not progress (manual 7.1).
